## Asian Giant Softshell Turtle

The Asian giant softshell turtle, also called the Yangtze giant softshell turtle, is one of the world’s rarest and most unusual reptiles. Its scientific name is *Rafetus swinhoei*. Unlike most turtles, it has a soft, leathery shell instead of a hard bony one. This adaptation helps it move through rivers and lakes more easily. It is also one of the largest freshwater turtles on Earth, and adults can grow very large and heavy (IUCN).

This turtle lives in freshwater habitats such as large rivers, lakes, and slow-moving streams. It is native to parts of China and Vietnam, but its population has dropped dramatically because of habitat loss, hunting, and pollution. Conservation groups consider it critically endangered, which means it is at extreme risk of extinction. In fact, only a few known individuals remain in the wild and in captivity (WWF).

The Asian giant softshell turtle plays an important role in its ecosystem. As an omnivore, it eats plants, fish, and other small animals, helping maintain balance in aquatic environments. Because it is so rare, protecting this species is important not only for biodiversity but also for preserving a unique part of nature’s history. Conservation efforts include habitat protection, breeding programs, and stronger wildlife laws. If these efforts succeed, this remarkable turtle may still have a chance to survive for future generations (Animal Diversity Web).

### Works Cited

IUCN. “*Rafetus swinhoei*.” *The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species*, https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/... Accessed 22 May 2026.

World Wildlife Fund. “Giant Softshell Turtle.” *WWF*, https://www.worldwildlife.org/. Accessed 22 May 2026.
